title: Phishing & Social Engineering Policy Template
metaDescription: Comprehensive policy template to protect your organization from phishing attacks and social engineering tactics. Ready-to-use format.
description: A comprehensive policy template designed to help organizations establish clear guidelines and procedures for identifying, preventing, and responding to phishing attacks and social engineering attempts.

sections.heading: Policy Overview and Scope
sections.content: This policy applies to all {{ORGANIZATION_NAME}} employees, contractors, and third-party users who access company systems or handle sensitive information. The purpose is to establish clear procedures for recognizing and responding to phishing attacks, social engineering attempts, and suspicious communications that could compromise organizational security.

sections.heading: Phishing Attack Recognition
sections.content: All personnel must be able to identify common phishing indicators including: urgent language demanding immediate action, suspicious sender addresses that don't match the claimed organization, generic greetings instead of personalized ones, requests for sensitive information via email, and mismatched or suspicious URLs. When in doubt, verify requests through independent communication channels before taking any action.

sections.heading: Email Security Procedures
sections.content: Employees must not click on suspicious links or download unexpected attachments. All emails requesting sensitive information, financial transactions, or system access must be verified through official company channels. Use secure browsers like Incognito Browser when accessing links from external sources. Report suspicious emails immediately to {{IT_CONTACT}} before deleting or forwarding.

sections.heading: Social Engineering Response
sections.content: Personnel should be cautious of unsolicited phone calls, in-person visits, or messages requesting confidential information or system access. Verify the identity of requesters through official company directories or callback procedures. Never provide passwords, system access, or sensitive data based solely on verbal requests, regardless of claimed authority or urgency.

sections.heading: Incident Reporting Procedures
sections.content: Suspected phishing attempts must be reported to {{SECURITY_TEAM}} within {{REPORTING_TIMEFRAME}} hours. Include the original email as an attachment, document any actions taken, and preserve evidence. Do not attempt to investigate suspicious communications independently. All incidents will be logged and analyzed to improve future prevention measures.

sections.heading: Training and Awareness Requirements
sections.content: All employees must complete phishing awareness training within {{TRAINING_PERIOD}} days of employment and annually thereafter. Training will include real-world examples, simulation exercises, and current threat intelligence. Department managers are responsible for ensuring their team's compliance and addressing any knowledge gaps identified during assessments.

sections.heading: Consequences and Enforcement
sections.content: Failure to follow this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination. However, employees who report suspected attacks in good faith will not face penalties, even if their actions inadvertently caused a security incident. The focus is on learning and improvement rather than punishment for honest mistakes.

sections.heading: Policy Review and Updates
sections.content: This policy will be reviewed annually by {{POLICY_OWNER}} and updated as needed to address emerging threats. All changes will be communicated to staff with appropriate training provided. The policy effective date is {{EFFECTIVE_DATE}} and supersedes all previous versions.

useCases: Small businesses establishing their first cybersecurity policies
HR departments creating employee security guidelines
Remote work teams needing clear security protocols
